transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, really. It's just a small thing, but my wife thought it would be best if I came in. 

I've just been having this little habit lately where I... well, I find myself checking things a few extra times. Just silly things, really, like the same boxes, or my daily lists, or the drawers around our condo. I'll just check them over and over before I feel like I can move on with my day. 

And the funny thing is, I know perfectly well I already looked. My poor wife will just be standing there, waiting for me to just leave it be so we can go. It's a bit embarrassing, honestly, making her wait over nothing. I try to stop, but I just like to be thorough, I suppose. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
Do you feel anxious or uneasy when you can't perform these checks?

Oh, anxious? No, I... I wouldn't use a strong word like that. I'm really not a nervous sort of fellow, honestly. 

I suppose I haven't really noticed feeling uneasy at all. If my wife is rushing me and I can't double-check, I just... well, I leave it be. I might prefer to give it one last look, just to be absolutely certain everything is in its place, but it doesn't upset me if I can't. 

I hope that's alright to say? I just don't want you to think I'm, you know, falling to pieces over a desk drawer or anything like that. I'm doing quite well, really. Does that sound fairly normal to you?
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or order?

A specific order? Um... no, I wouldn't say that, Doctor. Like I mentioned a moment ago, it's really just those same boxes, my daily lists, and the condo drawers. I just find myself checking them over and over before I feel like I can move on. 

There's no special routine to it, I promise. I just sort of go back to them, even though I know perfectly well I already looked and my poor wife is right there waiting for me to just leave it be. I just kind of flutter between them until I'm satisfied. I hope I'm not making it sound worse or more complicated than it is? It's really just a casual thing, no strict rules or anything like that. Did I answer your question alright?
Is this checking behavior causing any problems for you in your daily routine or relationships?

Well, problems... I wouldn't call them problems, exactly. It's just a bit of a nuisance, really. I mean, my wife and I recently moved, and... well, unpacking the condo has taken a little longer than it probably should have. Just because I get a bit caught up in making sure everything is sorted properly, you know? 

And, um, I suppose I have been putting off a few little things. I do some tutoring at the library, and I haven't quite gotten around to preparing for it lately. Or my hobbies, really. It just feels like I can't quite settle down to do those things until I'm sure the boxes and lists are, well, verified enough, I suppose. 

But it's nothing serious, I promise. Just a little delay in getting settled. I hope that doesn't sound too awful? I'm sure everyone gets a bit disorganized when they move, right?
Are you finding it harder to focus on your tutoring work at the library because of this checking behavior?

Well, I wouldn't say harder to focus, exactly. It's more just... finding the time to get to it, I suppose. 

As I mentioned, the unpacking at the new condo has just dragged on a bit longer than we anticipated. And because I feel like I need to make sure those boxes and my lists are, well, verified enough before I can really relax, I just haven't quite gotten around to preparing for the tutoring. Or my hobbies, for that matter. 

It's not that I can't focus on the tutoring itself once I'm there! It's just... I'm a bit delayed in getting my materials ready beforehand. I just like to have the house in order first, you know? That makes sense, doesn't it? I'm sure once the condo is fully unpacked, I'll be right back on track with the library. I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm neglecting my responsibilities?
Is your wife's reaction to your checking behavior causing any tension in your relationship with her?

Tension? Oh, no, no, not tension. I wouldn't use a strong word like that, Doctor. My wife is a wonderful woman, very patient. 

I mean, she might sigh a little bit now and then when I'm, you know, going over the drawers again, or maybe she'll tap her foot if we're trying to head out the door. Just normal spouse things, really! She's been very understanding about the move and everything taking a bit longer. 

We get along just fine, truly. I wouldn't want you to think I'm driving her crazy or anything like that. It's just a minor annoyance for her, I'm sure. I mean, it hasn't caused any real problems between us. Does that sound alright? I hope I haven't painted her in a bad light by mentioning she waits for me.
Are you avoiding any social activities because of your need to check these things?

Avoiding social activities? Oh, heavens, no. I wouldn't do that. 

I mean, since I retired, our social calendar isn't exactly packed to the brim anyway, but... no, we still see our friends. We might have another couple over for coffee, or go out to a nice dinner. I haven't canceled on anyone, I promise. 

I might, um, make us just a tiny bit late getting out the door sometimes, just double-checking the locks or the stove before we leave the condo, but I'd never just stay home to check things. That would be terribly rude to our friends, don't you think? I always make a point to keep my commitments. I hope you don't think I'm becoming a recluse or anything? We're still very much engaged with our social circle, truly.
Are you having trouble completing tasks at work or other responsibilities due to your need to check things?

Well, completing tasks... I wouldn't say I'm having *trouble*, exactly. I mean, I always get things done eventually. 

It's just that, as I might have mentioned before, the unpacking at the new condo is taking... well, a little longer than it probably should. I just want to make sure everything is put away perfectly, you know? So I have to check the boxes and my lists a few times. And because of that, I suppose I have been putting off getting my materials ready for the library tutoring. And my hobbies, too, I guess. 

It just feels like I can't really move on to those other things until I'm absolutely certain the condo is verified enough. But I'm still getting to it! I'm not just sitting around doing nothing. That's a normal way to handle a move, isn't it? Wanting to get the house settled before focusing on other things? I just want to make sure I'm doing it right.
Do you feel like things need to be arranged in a certain way or be symmetrical for you to consider them 'verified'?

Symmetrical? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't need things to be perfectly lined up or matching or anything like that. 

I mean, I just want things to be neat and tidy, of course. Just put away properly in the right boxes or drawers so I know where they are. It's not about making everything look like a magazine cover or having equal numbers of things on each side of the room. I'm not fussy like that! 

It's really just about knowing that the items I've unpacked are safely stored where they belong, so I don't lose anything in the shuffle of the new condo. That's a pretty reasonable way to organize, don't you think? Just keeping things orderly, rather than needing them to be perfectly symmetrical? I hope that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're trying to achieve a certain level of perfection when you're checking these things?

Perfection? Oh, my, no. I wouldn't call it perfection. That sounds so... well, so demanding, doesn't it? 

I really just want things to be, you know, settled. Just correct. I mean, when you move into a new place, you just want to feel sure that the stove is actually off and the doors are actually locked, right? It's not about being perfect, it's just about being safe and responsible. 

I suppose I do like to be thorough, yes. But I don't think I'm striving for some impossible standard of perfection. Just... peace of mind, really. That's a normal thing to want at my age, isn't it? Just to know things are secure? I certainly hope I don't come across as one of those overly rigid people. I just like to be careful, that's all.
Are you checking these things because you're worried something bad might happen if you don't?

Something bad? Oh, heavens, no. I wouldn't say I'm expecting a disaster or anything dramatic like that. I'm certainly not sitting around imagining fires or burglaries, if that's what you mean. 

I know some people get very worked up and paranoid about those sorts of things, but I really don't think I'm like that. It's more just... well, just a vague feeling of wanting to be sure things are settled. I don't have any terrible scenarios playing out in my head. I just think it's better to be safe than sorry, you know? 

Especially in a new building, you just want to be a good, responsible neighbor and make sure everything is locked up and turned off properly. It's just common sense, really, rather than being afraid of some catastrophe. That's a perfectly sensible way to look at it, don't you agree? I'm just trying to do the right thing.
Do you think something would go wrong or you would make a mistake if you didn't check these things?

A mistake? Oh, no, I wouldn't go that far. I mean, I've been managing my own affairs for a long, long time. I certainly don't think I've suddenly become careless or that I'm going to ruin something. 

It's not a fear of... of having done something wrong or making some foolish blunder. I just... well, I just like to be diligent. It's just a good habit to double-check, isn't it? Just to be absolutely certain. I don't feel like everything is going to fall apart if I don't look. I just prefer to follow my little routine before I settle in for the evening or leave the condo. 

I'm sure you see a lot of people my age who just like to stick to their routines, right? It's comforting. It just shows I still care about keeping a nice, orderly home, don't you think? I really try to be as responsible as I can.
Do you think you might overlook something important if you didn't check these things?

Overlook something important? Well... I suppose there is a bit of that, yes. But nothing extreme, I hope. 

It's just... well, since the move, I keep getting these nagging little thoughts. I'll be sitting in my chair, and it'll pop into my head that I might have accidentally thrown away something important from my old teaching files. Or maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box when I was sorting the garage out. 

I always tell myself it's highly unlikely—I was very organized with the packing, after all! But... the thought just sort of comes back anyway, and it makes it a little hard to just sit and settle for the evening. It sounds a bit foolish to be preoccupied with old lesson plans at my age, doesn't it? I just want to be sure I haven't lost track of anything useful. That's a fairly common thing to experience when you downsize, wouldn't you say? I certainly hope it doesn't make me sound scatterbrained.
Do you think your checking is related to concerns about making errors or mistakes?

Errors? Well... I suppose that's quite similar to what you asked just a moment ago, isn't it? I really don't think it's about making mistakes, no. 

I mean, having taught for so many years, I've always been rather trained to look out for errors on paper... but in my own daily life now? I certainly don't feel like I'm constantly making them or that I'm going to ruin anything. I just... well, I just like things to be correct and tidy. It's more about being thorough than being afraid of doing something wrong. 

That's a fairly normal trait for a retired fellow, wouldn't you agree? I certainly hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm incompetent or losing my touch. I really do try my best to stay sharp and handle my affairs properly.
Do you feel like you need to check these things to make sure you haven't forgotten something?

Forgotten something? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. My memory is still quite sharp, thankfully! 

I really don't feel like I'm checking because I've forgotten if I did something or not. I know I turned the stove off, for instance. It's not a memory issue at all. It's just... well, as I mentioned, it's just a matter of being thorough. A little extra glance just to be absolutely certain everything is exactly as it should be. 

I'm sure you meet plenty of folks my age who still have excellent recall, right? I really do pride myself on staying on top of things. I certainly don't want you to think I'm becoming forgetful or anything like that. That's just not the case at all.
Do you feel like you have to check these things even when you know it's not necessary?

Well... yes, I suppose that's the crux of it, isn't it? I do know it's not strictly necessary. 

That's actually what brought me in to see you, to be perfectly honest. I... I find myself checking the same moving boxes, my lists, the drawers in the new condo... just going over them again and again. And I know perfectly well I've already looked. I know it's fine. But I just can't seem to move on until I do it. 

My wife will be waiting for me, bless her, just telling me to leave it be and come sit down. And I want to, I really do. It's just a bit of a stubborn habit I've picked up, I suppose. I know it sounds a bit silly, a man my age fussing over drawers when he knows they're sorted. I do hope it doesn't make me sound entirely unreasonable. It's just a little quirk of adjusting to the new place, wouldn't you think?
Do you feel a strong sense of responsibility to ensure everything is in order, even when you know it's already been taken care of?

Responsibility? Oh, well... no, I wouldn't really say it's a sense of responsibility. It's not as though I feel the weight of the world on my shoulders, or that I'm the only one who can manage the new condo. 

My wife is perfectly capable, and she handles plenty of things beautifully! I certainly don't feel like it's my solemn duty to check on the boxes or the drawers. It's really just... well, just a personal preference for my own peace of mind, I suppose. Just my own little routine. 

I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm a control freak or trying to run the whole household, because I'm truly not. I just like things tidy for myself, just to feel settled. Does that make sense? I'd hate for you to think I'm being overbearing with my wife or taking on too much. That's really not the sort of husband I try to be.
Do you think something would be at risk if you didn't perform these checks?

At risk? Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. It's not as if I think... well, I certainly don't believe the condo is going to catch fire or that we'll be burgled just because I didn't look in a moving box one last time. I know we're perfectly safe. 

I really don't have any sort of fearful thoughts about disasters or anything of that nature. I'd hate for you to think I'm becoming paranoid in my old age, seeing dangers where there aren't any! I know some folks get a bit anxious about security as they get older, but I promise you that isn't me. 

It's truly just a matter of feeling settled, like I mentioned before. Just a little nagging feeling that goes away once I take a peek. That's fairly common when adjusting to a new environment, wouldn't you say? I just want to assure you I'm not sitting around worrying about terrible things happening to us.
Do you believe that if you didn't check these things, something would go wrong because of your own action or inaction?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I don't feel like I'm... well, I don't feel like I'm responsible for anything going wrong, or that my not checking would cause some sort of mishap. 

I know it might sound like I'm a bit neurotic, fussing over these things, but I promise I don't have any grand ideas that my actions are holding the universe together, or even just the household! I know perfectly well that whether I check a drawer or not, the sun will still rise and the condo will still be standing. 

It's really just a minor annoyance, this habit of mine. Just a little... a little tick, you might say, to get comfortable. I certainly hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that. It's quite normal to want things just so, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm explaining myself properly so you don't think worse of me.
Do you think your checking behavior is related to a fear of making mistakes or overlooking something important?

Well... I suppose... maybe a little bit? But it's not like I'm terrified of making a mistake, or that I think I'm losing my edge or anything like that! I was a teacher for many years, you know, and keeping track of things was just part of the job. 

It's just that lately, I keep getting these... well, these nagging thoughts. Just silly little worries that maybe I accidentally threw away something important from my old teaching files while we were packing, or maybe I put a needed tool in the wrong box and won't be able to find it. 

I know it's probably nonsense. I tell myself it's highly unlikely I'd do something so careless, but... the thought just keeps popping back into my head, and it makes it a bit hard to just sit down and relax. I'm sure it's very common to misplace things during a move, right? I just hope you don't think I'm becoming completely scatterbrained or obsessed with my old papers. It's just a bit of a nuisance, really. Does that sound like a normal reaction to moving?
